text:
Ellie Park: Hey team — vendor KoalaCloud Pty Ltd just sent an invoice for USD services and they've included a 10% GST line but no ABN on the invoice. They marked it as a tax invoice. Should we hold payment until we get ABN, or can we process and claim back? :thinking:

Tomas Alvarez: We normally need a valid ABN to accept GST charges for Australian vendors. Without it we risk not being able to claim input tax credits on our side. Also need the invoice to show ABN and GST breakdown.

Ellie Park: Got it — they've emailed saying they're GST-registered and provided an attachment called "GST_Certificate.pdf" (looks like a printout). Is that sufficient?

Priya Shah: Quick tax note: A certificate alone doesn't substitute for a proper ABN on the invoice. For ATO compliance the supplier should include their ABN and identify the amount of GST payable. If they truly are GST-registered but won't provide ABN, we should escalate.

Samir Gupta: Do we have any standing policy for refunds/gross-up when noncompliant invoices arrive? This vendor also asked for net USD after tax — they mentioned local PAYG withholding on non-resident contractors, but they're an Australian entity so PAYG doesn't apply for supplier invoices.

Tomas Alvarez: Right — PAYG withholding applies to payments to foreign residents for certain services. Since KoalaCloud is an Australian company, no foreign withholding. The only issue is GST on the invoice. If they lack ABN we may be required to withhold top-up amounts for certain payees, but that's not the case here.

Ellie Park: OK. I replied requesting: (1) supplier ABN to be printed on invoice, (2) corrected tax invoice format per ATO, and (3) confirmation their bank details match ABN. I told them we may delay payment until corrected doc is received.

Priya Shah: Also flag for procurement — if they can't produce ABN we should request a statutory declaration. And check whether their GST registration is active via ATO ABN lookup: https://abr.business.gov.au/ (paste vendor name and verify).

Samir Gupta: If they push back saying this is a SaaS subscription billed from AU but invoiced to Redwood US, any chance of reverse-charge or zero-rating?

Priya Shah: For B2B cross-border services, sometimes GST isn't charged (export of services) if the recipient is outside Australia and criteria met. But vendor charging GST indicates they believe it's taxable. We need them to justify. If they can show export of services rules apply, they'd remove GST and we can process without ABN, but they'd still ideally include ABN or note 'GST not applicable - export of services'.

Ellie Park: Payment-bot scheduled a reminder to follow up in 3 business days.

payment-bot: Reminder set: follow up with KoalaCloud (supplier invoice #KC-2026-042) in 72 hours.

Tomas Alvarez: Also logging this for month-end reconciliation — if we end up paying with GST and later it turns out vendor wasn't entitled to charge GST, we'll need a credit note and adjust the ledger.

Priya Shah: Last thing: if they insist on being paid net and ask Redwood to 'gross-up' to cover GST, we should decline unless approved by finance leadership. We don't gross-up routinely for supplier tax reporting differences.

Ellie Park: Thanks all — I'll update procurement and hold payment until we get corrected invoice or a clear justification for exported services. Will post update here when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
